question: If the speed of an object is doubled, its kinetic energy ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**becomes four times**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Kinetic Energy (K.E.)** is the energy possessed by an object by virtue of its **motion**. Every moving object, whether it is a falling grain of sand or a speeding planet, possesses some amount of kinetic energy.
 
• The standard mathematical formula for kinetic energy is **K.E. = 1/2 mv²**, where **m** represents the **mass** of the object and **v** represents its **velocity** or **speed**.
 
• In this formula, the **velocity** term is **squared**. This implies that the kinetic energy of an object is **directly proportional** to the **square of its speed**.
 
• When the speed of an object is **doubled** (v becomes **2v**), the new kinetic energy calculation becomes: **K.E_new = 1/2 m(2v)² = 1/2 m(4v²) = 4 * (1/2 mv²)**.
